analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the date, revises the GLM video description so variable-frame-rate video is indexed at i / nominalFrameRate rather than refused, and adds the native-tracked-engine output-control refusal and GLM logprob paragraphs. The head text I was given (lines 1613-2388) covers the reasoning/tool parsers, MiMo and Qwen4 sections, invariants and code map, plus the new text at 1732-1751. The earlier changed hunks at 810-829 and 876-895 were visible only as patch excerpts.

I found no concrete security regression and no code or control change.

The new text at lines 1732-1742 describes a fail-closed pre-reservation refusal. EngineV2Bridge.nativeOutputControlRefusal returns a 400 client_error for token constraints and unsupported logprob rows on native-tracked engines. It avoids a 500 generation_failure that would strike the inference-error breaker (relates to T-010 and availability). This is a documented behavior, not a weakening. Lines 1744-1750 say a GLM logprob row never drafts or verifies, and that the whole step decodes target-only while such a row runs beside other rows. This is a minor performance and availability note with no confidentiality impact.

The doc claim that GLM variable-frame-rate video is now accepted and indexed is a behavior change visible only in the patch excerpt. It is not backed by source here. It could widen the media-decoding attack surface (decoded-frame cap 512 MiB, 28,532 visual-token cap), but the caps stay documented and the code is not supplied. The next pass should check that GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset enforces the frame and byte bounds and the media reservation for VFR tracks, and that VFR frame-count or timing manipulation cannot exceed them.

Lines 1732-1751 are consistent with the T-041 prefix-cache posture. They cite no cache-scope or at-rest changes, and the cache-identity statement at lines 1729-1730 is unchanged.

I did not verify the cited source files for any claim.
